q: What's on the timeline toolbar of the Edit page in the Resolve workflow?
a: From left to right: the tools **Selection** (A), **Trim** (T) and **Blade** (B); the edits **Insert** (F9), **Overwrite** (F10) and **Replace** (F11), which put the Source Viewer's clip (its In and Out) at the timeline's In mark, or at the playhead; the toggles **Snapping**, **Linked Selection** and **Add Marker**; and on the right **Full Extent Zoom**, **Detail Zoom** around the playhead, zoom out, the zoom slider and zoom in. It replaces the Tools strip beside the timeline; the Premiere workflow keeps the Tools strip.

q: I liked Premiere's Tools panel. Can I get it back?
a: Yes, by working in the Premiere workflow (Settings ▸ General ▸ Workflow): it keeps the Tools strip beside the timeline. In the DaVinci Resolve workflow the same tools sit on Resolve's toolbar across the top of the timeline instead: Selection (A), Trim (T) and Blade (B), with Snapping and Linked Selection further along. Neither is better; pick the one whose layout your hands already know.

q: how do i split clips with the blade on the resolve edit page
a: Pick **Blade** on the left of the timeline toolbar (or press B), then click a clip where you want the cut. Press A (or click **Selection**) to go back to moving clips.

q: Drop the take I marked in the Source Viewer into the timeline at the playhead without pushing anything later, on the Edit page.
a:
1. In the Source Viewer, set In and Out on the take.
2. Make sure the timeline has no In mark (with one, the edit goes there instead) and park the playhead where the take should start.
3. Click **Overwrite** on the timeline toolbar (F10; command `edit.overwrite`). The take covers what is under it and nothing later moves.
Use **Insert** (F9, `edit.insert`) instead when you want the rest of the timeline pushed later, and **Replace** (F11, `edit.replace`) to swap a clip.

q: What do the zoom controls on the right of the Edit page's timeline toolbar do?
a: **Full Extent Zoom** fits the whole timeline in view, **Detail Zoom** zooms in around the playhead, and zoom out, the zoom slider and zoom in step the zoom by hand.

q: Explain the Resolve-style track header to me.
a: Its top line has the source patch and the track's badge (V1, A1: lit when the track is targeted), then the lock, sync lock and the output / mute / solo switches. Under it are the track's name and how many clips it holds.

q: Which transport buttons do the viewers have in the Resolve workflow?
a: Resolve's set: first frame, play reverse, stop, play, last frame, loop, then Mark In and Mark Out. The other buttons Revolution has (frame steps and so on) aren't drawn there but stay on their keys and menus.

q: My Media Pool has a list down its left with Master at the top. What is it?
a: That's the **Bins** column of the Resolve layout: Master, then every bin in the project. Click a bin to show only its clips; click Master to see everything again.

q: and how do I drop a marker from that toolbar?
a: Click **Add Marker** among the toggles in the middle of the timeline toolbar (or press M; command `markers.add`). It sits next to Snapping and Linked Selection.

context.q: how do I turn snapping off on the resolve edit page
context.a: Click Snapping on the timeline toolbar so it is no longer lit; click it again to turn it back on.
